messages:
emily: Quick FYI — onboarding reports point to three tiny docs bugs that are causing copy/paste friction for new signups:
emily: 1) README Ruby quickstart uses `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY` inside double quotes which cmd/CMD.exe users paste incorrectly (percent vars needed).
emily: 2) The Ruby sample still uses the old client call `client.chat(message)` instead of the new responses API. Leads to NoMethodError.
emily: 3) The curl example in quickstart uses backslash continuations which GitHub soft-wraps and breaks for folks on mobile or when copying into PowerShell.

emily: Current Ruby snippet in docs:

emily: ```ruby
require 'net/http'
require 'json'
uri = URI('https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses')
req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
req['Content-Type'] = "application/json"
req['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}"
req.body = { input: 'hello' }.to_json
res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, use_ssl: true) { |http| http.request(req) }
puts JSON.parse(res.body)
```

emily: That snippet is fine for POSIX shells, but our Windows docs show the same and people paste into cmd where %REDWOOD_API_KEY% is required. Also some older Ruby examples in the repo still call `client.chat` (legacy).

jared: Agreed. Proposed fixes: replace multi-line curl with a one-liner example, add a Windows cmd curl variant and a PowerShell Invoke-RestMethod example, and update Ruby sample to demonstrate the official SDK usage (responses.create) plus a minimal net/http example with clear ENV guidance.

jared: One-liner curl (cross-shell friendly):

jared: ```
curl -sS --header 'Content-Type: application/json' --header "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw '{"input":"hello"}'
```

jared: Windows cmd variant (note %VAR%):

jared: ```
set REDWOOD_API_KEY=your_key_here
curl -sS --header "Content-Type: application/json" --header "Authorization: Bearer %REDWOOD_API_KEY%" https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses --data-raw "{\"input\":\"hello\"}"
```

jared: Ruby SDK canonical example (uses responses.create):

jared: ```ruby
require 'redwood' # gem name placeholder
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.responses.create(input: 'hello')
puts resp.output
```

leah: Also noticed the Go quickstart has an old import path `github.com/redwood/sdk` in one example; should be `github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go` per our latest releases. I'll scan and list remaining mismatches in the PR.

support-bot: Created issue #6123: "docs: quickstart - fix Ruby/curl Windows quoting, update SDK snippets to responses.create, and audit import paths"  https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/6123

emily: I'll open a small PR with the one-liner, Windows/PowerShell examples, updated Ruby SDK/net-http snippet, and a short Troubleshooting note about shell variable syntax and fish users. Will tag @leah for import-path audit.

jared: Happy to review the PR. :thumbsup:

emily: Thanks — shipping this should reduce a bunch of noisy support tickets.
